title: Understated Umami Chinese Pork Bao
description: A salty, bouncy-qq, sick-day Chinese dish featuring rosemary, served in a donabe, this kosher-friendly recipe is perfect for a comforting meal. It originates from Jiangsu cuisine.
instructions: Preheat the donabe over medium heat.
Heat the vegetable oil in the donabe and sear the pork shoulder until browned on all sides.
Add the sliced ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the soy sauce, sesame oil, salt, and black pepper, and stir to combine.
Add the brine-wet pork shoulder back to the donabe and cook for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, prepare the bao dough according to the package instructions.
Assemble the bao by placing a portion of the pork mixture onto a dough circle and topping with chopped green onions and a sprig of rosemary.
Serve the Understated Umami Chinese Pork Bao hot.
Garnish with additional green onions and rosemary if desired.
